I liked that the lights didnt just turn on and off, they gradually got brighter as I turned the dial which helped me see what it was doing better before I added the LED into the breadboard.
The corresponding  LED's on the shield light up depending on the used pin. When the potentiometer is towards the very top of the values other LED's on the Shield light up but I'm not really sure why

The shield made it easy to understand where the power was going on the Arduino, all the LEDs on the analog side were all lit up which signalled to me that they were all receiving power. As I was turning the dial it was easy to see the resistance in the board itself as the lights of the shield were fading, this was corresponding with the breadboard and the LED I had set up.

The lights on the shield really help indicate what parts of the Aurduino are connected and using power. There is a bit of noise that makes the analog lights turn on which is slightly misleading but as long as you keep noise in mind, it is quite easy to grasp what's happening within the written code and the output from it. The lights turning on when the button is pressed makes it very easy to understand that the LED on the breadboard will be turning on too.
I find having visual feedback of the pin activity helps with understanding how the flow or the signals works and made it easy to identify the signal pathways at play.

Though the sandbox nature of this exercise I've quickly learnt how code can compile with no errors and look fine at first but not give the result we want or expect. Through the use of p5js we've seen this in action and experimented with how live preview type coding can really help defend against functional errors that tilt on only one line of code.

This exercise efficiently shows how p5js' layering works though it's compilation. By simply taking the last two lines of the draw function and placing them in the middle of the function (line 11) we completely change the side affect of the function. I've learnt how we can easily have the right code for our goal but it might just be layered or ordered wrongly.
